description.text:
This is a private Gamescope protocol. Regular Wayland clients must not use
it.

This constructor only enables the original past_present_timing,
refresh_cycle and retired events, regardless of the bound version.
Clients must use create_swapchain_with_timing to opt into newer events.

Creates a swapchain that also receives present_timing and
timing_properties. Binding version 2 alone does not enable these
events, since older clients may bind the advertised version without
understanding them. The initial properties arrive once the compositor
knows the surface's timing.
description.summary: create a swapchain with presentation timing events

description.text:
Xwayland creates a wl_surface for each X11 window. It sends a
WL_SURFACE_ID client message to indicate the mapping between the X11
windows and the wl_surface objects.

This request overrides this mapping for a given X11 window, allowing an
X11 client to submit buffers via the Wayland protocol. The override
only affects buffer submission. Everything else (e.g. input events)
still uses Xwayland's WL_SURFACE_ID.

x11_server is gotten by the GAMESCOPE_XWAYLAND_SERVER_ID property on the
root window of the associated server.

Provide swapchain feedback to the compositor.

This is what the useless tearing protocol should have been.
Absolutely not enough information in the final protocol to do what we want for SteamOS --
which is have the Allow Tearing toggle apply to *both* Mailbox + Immediate and NOT fifo,
essentially acting as an override for tearing on/off for games.
The upstream protocol is very useless for our usecase here.

Provides image count ahead of time instead of needing to try and calculate it from
an initial stall if we are doing low latency.

Provides colorspace info for us to do HDR for both HDR10 PQ and scRGB.
The upstream HDR efforts seem to have no interest in supporting scRGB but we *need* that so /shrug
We can do it here now! Yipee!

Swapchain feedback solves so many problems! :D

Forward HDR metadata from Vulkan to the compositor.

HDR Metadata Infoframe as per CTA 861.G spec.
This is expected to match exactly with the spec.

display_primary_*:
Color Primaries of the Data.
Specifies X and Y coordinates.
These are coded as unsigned 16-bit values in units of
0.00002, where 0x0000 represents zero and 0xC350
represents 1.0000.

white_point_*:
White Point of Colorspace Data.
Specifies X and Y coordinates.
These are coded as unsigned 16-bit values in units of
0.00002, where 0x0000 represents zero and 0xC350
represents 1.0000.

max_display_mastering_luminance:
Max Mastering Display Luminance.
This value is coded as an unsigned 16-bit value in units of 1 cd/m2,
where 0x0001 represents 1 cd/m2 and 0xFFFF represents 65535 cd/m2.

max_display_mastering_luminance:
Min Mastering Display Luminance.
This value is coded as an unsigned 16-bit value in units of
0.0001 cd/m2, where 0x0001 represents 0.0001 cd/m2 and 0xFFFF
represents 6.5535 cd/m2.

max_cll:
Max Content Light Level.
This value is coded as an unsigned 16-bit value in units of 1 cd/m2,
where 0x0001 represents 1 cd/m2 and 0xFFFF represents 65535 cd/m2.

max_fall:
Max Frame Average Light Level.
This value is coded as an unsigned 16-bit value in units of 1 cd/m2,
where 0x0001 represents 1 cd/m2 and 0xFFFF represents 65535 cd/m2.
description.summary: set HDR metadata for a surface

description.text:
Sets the display timing of the next commit.

This gets reset to 0s in the compositor's state after a commit.

args.name: desired_present_time_hi
args.summary: high part of the desired presentation time for this commit. Uses CLOCK_MONOTONIC. 0 = present as soon as possible.

args.name: desired_present_time_lo
args.summary: low part of the desired presentation time for this commit. Uses CLOCK_MONOTONIC. 0 = present as soon as possible.

description.text:
Only swapchains created with create_swapchain_with_timing accept this
request. Other swapchains ignore it, including zero-serial requests.
Registers a client-local serial for one timing report. Target uses
CLOCK_MONOTONIC nanoseconds, or a duration with the relative flag. Zero
requests presentation as soon as possible, as does a relative target
before this swapchain has latched a frame. Unknown flag bits are ignored.
The request applies to the next commit that carries buffer content,
including one that recommits the current buffer. Replacing an armed
serial reports the old serial as dropped. A zero serial clears any
armed request and is never reported.
description.summary: timing request for the next commit

args.name: serial_hi
args.summary: high part of the client timing serial

args.name: serial_lo
args.summary: low part of the client timing serial

args.name: target_hi
args.summary: high part of target time or relative duration in nanoseconds

args.name: target_lo
args.summary: low part of target time or relative duration in nanoseconds

description.text: Gives information on the past presentation timing

args.name: present_margin_lo

description.text: Gives information on the refresh cycle for this swapchain
description.summary: information about refresh cycle for this swapchain

args.name: refresh_cycle_hi
args.summary: high part of the refresh cycle in nanos

args.name: refresh_cycle_lo
args.summary: low part of the refresh cycle in nanos

description.text:
Only sent to swapchains created with create_swapchain_with_timing.
Sent once per serial when presented or dropped, unless this object is
destroyed first. All timestamps use CLOCK_MONOTONIC nanoseconds. Zero
means unavailable, and a dropped commit has all timestamps zero. Pixel
out is the compositor's predicted scanout.
description.summary: timing result for the registering swapchain

args.name: serial_hi
args.summary: high part of the client timing serial

args.name: serial_lo
args.summary: low part of the client timing serial

args.name: queue_end_hi
args.summary: high part of queue completion time in nanoseconds

args.name: queue_end_lo
args.summary: low part of queue completion time in nanoseconds

args.name: dequeued_hi
args.summary: high part of latch time in nanoseconds

args.name: dequeued_lo
args.summary: low part of latch time in nanoseconds

args.name: pixel_out_hi
args.summary: high part of predicted scanout time in nanoseconds

args.name: pixel_out_lo
args.summary: low part of predicted scanout time in nanoseconds

description.text:
Only sent to swapchains created with create_swapchain_with_timing.
Duration is the effective cycle including the frame limiter, the same
value refresh_cycle carries. Interval is the panel cycle on fixed
refresh, or UINT64_MAX for variable refresh.
Sent once the compositor knows the window's timing and whenever the
values change. Until then both values are unknown to the client.

args.name: refresh_duration_hi
args.summary: high part of effective refresh duration in nanoseconds

args.name: refresh_duration_lo
args.summary: low part of effective refresh duration in nanoseconds

args.name: refresh_interval_hi
args.summary: high part of base refresh interval in nanoseconds

args.name: refresh_interval_lo
args.summary: low part of base refresh interval in nanoseconds

entries.name: relative
entries.summary: target is a duration after this swapchain's previous expected scanout

entries.name: nearest_refresh_cycle
entries.summary: allow presentation less than half an effective refresh cycle early
